results.guarantee: E μ(H∩Gₚ) ≥ (1−ε) E μ(Gₚ), for ε∈(0,1)
results.sourceLocation: Section 4, Theorem 1 and Sample-and-Union Algorithm 1; §1 Result 1
results.notes: Preprint v1: theorem statement checked; proof not independently verified. Sample-and-union takes R independent simulated realizations and unions one maximum matching from each; Δ(H)≤R. The budget is polynomial jointly in 1/ε and 1/p. Remark 4.1 states that a refined analysis of the same efficient sample-and-union algorithm gives O(log(1/ε)·(1/(p ε²)+1/ε³)); the plotted point retains numbered Theorem 1. Appendix B removes the logarithmic factor using a different construction with exact edge-selection marginals, giving O(1/(p ε²)+1/ε³), but claims no efficient exact computation of those marginals. The guarantee is unweighted and non-adaptive, not a weighted or adaptive-testing theorem. Finite simple undirected general unweighted graph; every edge survives independently with the same known p∈(0,1] Ratio of expectations over independent test-edge realizations and the algorithm’s independent simulations; no high-probability approximation statement
